main_text.p: iuncta uigilantia imitati essent, aut nunc imitarentur maiores nostri, inculpatius equidē, ut opinor, cū Christianorū moribus ageretur, simul & fatale hanc malorū tempestatem, quibus tā misere hodie cōcutitur anglię imp. aut nō incidissemus, aut adhuc propelleremus. Nūc uero dū augurijs attendunt Principes, Episcopi ἱερεῖς, ambitione insaniunt theologi, occidūtur prophetę. Magnates lasciuiūt, cōniuent magistratus, uulgus in oēm ruit licentiā, stupra, repudia, adulteria, auaritia, fraus, temulentia, cōtentio, crapula, usura, periuria, cū omni deniq; uitiorū segete, uelut effractis claustris, qua data porta ruit: quid mirū, si luxatis undiq; reip. cōpagibus, ruinā demū ac περιπατεῖν spectare omnia uideantur. Atq; hactenus satis opinor malis miserīsque edocti edidicimus, quid sit in manus Domini incidere, quid sit abuti Euangelio ipsius. Tempus nūc postulat, ut pertæsi corruptelas

page.notes: Greek words in the text ("ἱερεῖς", "περιπατεῖν") are transcribed from a small-type rendering and may be imperfect; "ἱερεῖς" and "περιπατεῖν" are uncertain readings. The first line of text reads "iuncta" and the page has no catchword or signature.
